question:
In the adjoining figure, \(CD\) is the diameter of a semicircle with center \(O.\) Point \(A\) lies on the extension of \(DC\) past \(C;\) point \(E\) lies on the semicircle, and \(B\) is the point of intersection (distinct from \(E\)) of line segment \(AE\) with the semicircle. If length \(AB\) equals length \(OD,\) and the measure of \(\angle EOD\) is \(45^\circ,\) then the measure of \(\angle BAO\) is

[Figure 1](figures/1979_AMC_12_Q12_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The condition \(AB=OD\) connects the secant segment to a radius. Joining \(O\) to \(B\) reveals two isosceles triangles, because
\[
AB=OB=OE=OD.
\]
Let \(x=\angle BAO\). In triangle \(ABO\), the equality \(AB=OB\) gives \(\angle AOB=x\). Hence
\[
\angle ABO=180^\circ-2x.
\]
Point \(B\) lies between \(A\) and \(E\), so rays \(BA\) and \(BE\) point in opposite directions. Consequently,
\[
\angle OBE=180^\circ-\angle ABO=2x.
\]
Now \(OB=OE\), so triangle \(OBE\) has equal base angles and \(\angle BEO=2x\). Rays \(EB\) and \(EA\) coincide, giving \(\angle AEO=2x\).

Also, rays \(OA\) and \(OD\) are opposite, so
\[
\angle AOE=180^\circ-45^\circ=135^\circ.
\]
Since rays \(AB\) and \(AE\) coincide, the angle at \(A\) in triangle \(AOE\) is \(x\). Its angle sum gives
\[
x+2x+135^\circ=180^\circ,
\qquad 3x=45^\circ,
\qquad x=15^\circ.
\]
Thus \(\angle BAO=15^\circ\), choice \(\boxed{B}\).
